name: DIFC Employment Law (DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019)
description: Employment terms under the DIFC Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019, as amended (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025): the articles an employment contract in the DIFC must meet. English is the language of DIFC legislation. DRAFT: not yet legally reviewed.

clauses.title: No waiver: minimum requirements, no waiver
clauses.content: The requirements of this Law are minimum requirements and a provision in an agreement to waive any of those requirements, except where expressly permitted under this Law, is void in all circumstances.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)
clauses.guidance: A contract term that waives any requirement of the Law is void, unless the Law expressly allows it.

clauses.title: No waiver: more favourable terms and settlement agreements
clauses.content:
Nothing in this Law precludes:
(a) an Employer from providing in any Employment Contract terms and conditions that are more favourable to an Employee than those required by this Law; or
(b) subject to Article 66(13), an Employee from waiving any right, remedy, obligation, claim or action under this Law by entering into a written agreement with their Employer to terminate their employment or to resolve a dispute with their Employer, provided:
(i) the Employee warrants in the written agreement that they were given an opportunity to receive independent legal advice from a Legal Practitioner as to the terms and effect of the written agreement; or
(ii) the Employer and Employee took part in mediation proceedings provided by the Court prior to entering into the written agreement.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: No false representations
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Hiring children
clauses.content: An Employer shall not employ a child who is under sixteen (16) years of age. An Employer who contravenes this provision is liable to a fine as set out in Schedule 2.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Right to a written contract: written contract in English within seven days
clauses.content: An Employer shall provide an Employee with a written Employment Contract in the English language within seven (7) days of the commencement of the Employee's employment with the Employer.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Right to a written contract: what the contract must include
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)
clauses.guidance: The contract must include: names of the parties; start date; wage; pay period; hours and days of work; vacation leave; notice for each party; job title; indefinite or fixed term (and end date); place of work; disciplinary and grievance rules; probation of at most six months; applicable policies.

clauses.title: Right to a written contract: amendments in writing
clauses.content: Any amendment to an Employment Contract must be in writing and signed by both the Employer and Employee, unless such amendment is of an administrative nature only, in which case the Employer shall be required to record such amendment in writing and to give written notice thereof to the Employee prior to the amendment taking effect.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Itemised pay statements: itemised pay statements
clauses.content:
An Employee is entitled to receive as soon as reasonably practicable a written itemised pay statement in respect of each Pay Period that includes:
(a) the amount of the Remuneration payable; and
(b) the amount of any deduction from that amount and the purpose for which it is made.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Paydays: pay within seven days of the pay period
clauses.content: Subject to Articles 18(2), 20 and 28(2), an Employer shall pay to an Employee all Remuneration earned by the Employee in a Pay Period within seven (7) days after the end of the Pay Period.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Paydays: deferred additional payments
clauses.content: Payment of any Additional Payments may be deferred and subject to other conditions by written agreement between the Employer and Employee.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Payments following termination: payments within fourteen days of termination
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Payments following termination: late payment penalty
clauses.content: Subject to the provisions of Article 19(3) and 19(4), an Employee shall be entitled to and the Employer shall pay a penalty equal to an Employee’s Daily Wage for each day the Employer is in arrears of its payment obligations under Article 19(1).
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Deductions: permitted deductions
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Recruitment costs: no charges for recruitment
clauses.content:
An Employer shall not request, charge or receive, directly or indirectly, from a person seeking employment, a payment for:
(a) employing or obtaining employment for the person seeking employment; or
(b) providing information about Employers seeking Employees.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Recruitment costs: no recovery of recruitment costs
clauses.content: Subject to Article 21(3), an Employer is not permitted to recoup from an Employee any costs or expenses incurred by the Employer in the course of recruiting the Employee.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Recruitment costs: recovery on early resignation
clauses.content:
If an Employee terminates their Employment Contract for any reason other than termination for cause under Article 63, and their Termination Date falls within a period of six (6) months from the Employee's date of commencement of employment, the Employer may, subject to Article 57(2), recoup from the Employee such reasonable costs or expenses which:
(a) were directly incurred by the Employer in the course of recruiting the Employee;
(b) are supported by proof of expenditure provided by the Employer to the Employee; and
(c) are specified in the Employment Contract as being payable by the Employee to the Employer in such circumstances.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Maximum weekly working time
clauses.content: An Employee's working time shall not exceed an average of forty-eight (48) hours for each seven (7) day period during the Relevant Calculation Period unless the Employer has first obtained the Employee's consent in writing.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)
clauses.guidance: Working time may not exceed an average of 48 hours a week over the calculation period unless the employee has first agreed in writing.

clauses.title: Ramadan
clauses.content: During the holy month of Ramadan, a Muslim Employee shall not be required to work in excess of six (6) hours each day. There shall be no reduction in an Employee’s Wage as a result of the Employee's reduced working hours.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Daily rest
clauses.content: An Employee is entitled to a rest period of not less than eleven (11) consecutive hours in each twenty-four (24) hour period.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Weekly rest period
clauses.content: An Employee is entitled to an uninterrupted rest period of not less than twenty-four (24) hours in each seven (7) day period.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Breaks: rest and prayer breaks
clauses.content: Where the working time for an Employee during a Work Day exceeds six (6) hours, the Employee is entitled to rest and prayer breaks of at least one (1) hour in aggregate during the Work Day.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Vacation Leave: twenty work days a year
clauses.content: Subject to Article 30, an Employee who has been employed for at least ninety (90) days is entitled to paid Vacation Leave of twenty (20) Work Days in each Vacation Leave Year.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)
clauses.guidance: At least 20 work days of paid vacation leave a year once employed for 90 days.

clauses.title: Vacation Leave: carrying leave forward
clauses.content: An Employee is entitled to carry forward accrued but untaken Vacation Leave into the next Vacation Leave Year for a maximum period of twelve (12) months after which any unused Vacation Leave shall expire. The amount of accrued but untaken Vacation Leave to be carried forward may be agreed between the Employer and Employee, provided that nothing shall preclude an Employee from rolling over at least five (5) Work Days per Vacation Leave Year.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Vacation Leave: no payment in lieu without agreement
clauses.content: Unless otherwise agreed in writing by an Employee, and subject to Article 28(1), an Employee cannot receive payment in lieu of Vacation Leave.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Compensation in lieu of Vacation Leave: payment for untaken leave on termination
clauses.content: Where an Employee's employment is terminated, the Employer shall pay the Employee an amount in lieu of Vacation Leave accrued but not taken up to and including the Termination Date calculated in accordance with Article 28(3).
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Dates of Vacation Leave: leave dates set by the employer
clauses.content: The Employer may require an Employee to take Vacation Leave on specified days in the current Vacation Leave Year by giving at least seven (7) days prior written notice to the Employee.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Vacation Leave during first year of employment
clauses.content:
(1) During the first year of employment, the amount of Vacation Leave an Employee may take is limited to the remaining amount of Vacation Leave accrued by the Employee at the time of taking such Vacation Leave in accordance with Article 30(2).
(2) Vacation Leave accrues during an Employee's first year of employment on a monthly basis at the rate of one-twelfth (1/12) of the Employee's annual entitlement to Vacation Leave.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Public Holidays and pay: public holidays
clauses.content: An Employee is entitled to leave on each Public Holiday that is announced in the UAE by the relevant Competent Authority for the public sector or the private sector, whichever is applicable to the Employee's Employer, which falls on a Work Day.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Public Holidays and pay: work on a public holiday
clauses.content:
If an Employee agrees to work on a Public Holiday, in addition to their Daily Wage under Article 32(2), the Employer must provide the Employee with either:
(a) a day of leave in lieu of each Public Holiday worked;
(b) payment of an amount equal to the Employee’s Daily Wage for the Public Holiday worked; or
(c) payment of a pro-rated amount of the Employee’s Daily Wage based on the time period worked during the Public Holiday.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Special Leave
clauses.content: A Muslim Employee, who has completed at least one (1) year of continuous employment with an Employer, shall be entitled to special unpaid leave not exceeding twenty-one (21) days to perform the Hajj pilgrimage once during the period of their employment with the Employer.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Sick Leave: sixty work days a year
clauses.content: An Employee is entitled to Sick Leave of sixty (60) consecutive or intermittent Work Days in aggregate in a twelve (12) month period. Any references in Articles 35 and 36 to a twelve (12) month period shall be deemed to be the same period as referred to in this Article 34(1).
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Sick Pay: sick pay
clauses.content:
Subject to the Employee's compliance with Article 34(2), an Employer shall pay Sick Pay to an Employee at:
(a) one hundred percent (100%) of the Employee's Daily Wage for the first ten (10) Work Days of Sick Leave taken in a twelve (12) month period; and
(b) fifty percent (50%) of the Employee's Daily Wage for the next twenty (20) Work Days of Sick Leave taken in the same twelve (12) month period.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Excessive Sick Leave: termination for excessive sick leave
clauses.content: Where an Employee takes more than an aggregate of sixty (60) Work Days of Sick Leave in a twelve (12) month period, the Employer may terminate the Employment Contract with immediate effect on written notice to the Employee.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Maternity Leave: sixty-five work days
clauses.content: A female Employee may take Maternity Leave of up to sixty-five (65) Work Days.
clauses.section: Part 5: Parental Leave And Related Rights
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Maternity Leave: eligibility for maternity pay
clauses.section: Part 5: Parental Leave And Related Rights
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Maternity Pay: maternity pay
clauses.content:
An Employer shall pay Maternity Pay to an Employee pursuant to Article 37(2) at:
(a) one hundred percent (100%) of the Employee’s Daily Wage for the first thirty-three (33) Work Days of Maternity Leave; and
(b) fifty percent (50%) of the Employee’s Daily Wage for the next thirty-two (32) Work Days of Maternity Leave.
clauses.section: Part 5: Parental Leave And Related Rights
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Paternity Leave and pay: paternity leave
clauses.content:
A male Employee may take Paternity Leave of up to five (5) Work Days if he:
(a) will have been continuously employed by his Employer for at least twelve (12) months, including any period of Secondment, immediately preceding the expected or actual week of his wife giving birth; and
(b) notifies his Employer in writing that his wife is pregnant at least eight (8) weeks before the expected week of childbirth.
clauses.section: Part 5: Parental Leave And Related Rights
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Right to return to work: no dismissal for pregnancy or parental leave
clauses.content:
An Employer shall not, because of an Employee's pregnancy or Parental Leave:
(a) terminate the Employee’s employment; or
(b) change the Employee’s position or terms and conditions of employment without the Employee's prior written consent.
clauses.section: Part 5: Parental Leave And Related Rights
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Right to return to work: return to the same role
clauses.content: An Employee has the right to return to work at the end of Parental Leave to the same or a substantially similar role on the same terms and conditions of employment and with the same level of seniority the Employee had immediately prior to taking Parental Leave.
clauses.section: Part 5: Parental Leave And Related Rights
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Health insurance
clauses.content: An Employer is required to obtain and maintain health insurance cover for each of its Employees as may be required pursuant to the Regulations, Federal Law or Dubai Law. An Employer who contravenes this provision is liable to a fine as set out in Schedule 2.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Visas and permits: visas and permits at the employer’s cost
clauses.content: If an Employee is required to work in the DIFC, their Employer is required to obtain and maintain, at the Employer's own cost, the requisite sponsorship documentation (including UAE and DIFC identity documentation), visas, authorisations, licenses, permits and approvals as may be required from time to time by Federal Law, Dubai Law, a Competent Authority or a Personnel Sponsorship Agreement, to enable the Employee to work lawfully for the Employer in the DIFC and comply with any such requirements.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Visas and permits: no recovery of visa costs or retention of passports
clauses.content:
An Employer is not permitted to:
(a) recoup any costs and expenses incurred pursuant to Article 57(1) from an Employee; or
(b) retain the passport or other original personal documents of an Employee.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Discrimination: prohibited grounds
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Victimisation
clauses.content:
(1) An Employer must not victimise an Employee.
(2) For the purposes of this Part 9, an Employer victimises an Employee if it subjects the Employee to a detriment or dismisses him because the Employee does a protected act, or the Employer believes that the Employee has done, or may do, a protected act. Each of the following is a protected act:
(a) bringing proceedings under this Part 9;
(b) giving evidence or information in connection with proceedings under this Part 9;
(c) doing any other thing for the purposes of or in connection with this Part 9; and
(d) making an allegation (whether or not express) that the Employer or another person has contravened this Part 9.
(3) Giving false evidence or information, or making a false allegation, is not a protected act under Article 60(2) if the evidence or information is given, or the allegation is made, in bad faith.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Minimum notice periods: minimum notice periods
clauses.content:
Subject to Articles 62(3), 62(4), 62(6) and 63, the written notice required to be given by an Employer or Employee to terminate the Employee’s employment shall not be less than:
(a) seven (7) days, if the period of continuous employment of the Employee is less than three (3) months, including any period of Secondment;
(b) thirty (30) days, if the period of continuous employment of the Employee is in excess of three (3) months but less than five (5) years, including any period of Secondment; or
(c) ninety (90) days, if the period of continuous employment of the Employee is in excess of five (5) years, including any period of Secondment.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)
clauses.guidance: Minimum written notice: 7 days with under three months of service, 30 days from three months to five years, 90 days beyond five years; it doesn’t apply during probation or to the agreed end of a fixed term.

clauses.title: Minimum notice periods: longer notice by agreement
clauses.content: Article 62(2) shall not prevent an Employer and Employee from agreeing to a longer notice period in an Employment Contract.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Minimum notice periods: pay in lieu of notice
clauses.content: An Employer may only make a payment of Wages to an Employee in lieu of all or part of the Employee's notice period pursuant to Article 63(2) or if the Employee agrees to such a payment in an agreement entered into pursuant to Article 11(2)(b).
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Minimum notice periods: when the minimum notice does not apply
clauses.content:
Article 62(2) does not apply:
(a) during any probation period agreed in an Employment Contract;
(b) where it has been agreed in the Employment Contract that the Employee's employment will terminate on the expiry of a fixed term; or
(c) in respect of termination for excessive Sick Leave in accordance with Article 36(1).
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Termination for cause: termination for cause
clauses.content: An Employer or an Employee may terminate an Employee’s employment with immediate effect for cause in circumstances where the conduct of one (1) party warrants termination and where a reasonable Employer or Employee would have terminated the employment as a consequence thereof.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Termination for cause: employee’s entitlements after resigning for cause
clauses.content:
If an Employee terminates their employment for cause pursuant to Article 63(1), the Employee shall be entitled to:
(a) a payment of Wages in lieu of their notice period;
(b) a Gratuity Payment calculated to include the notice period the Employee would have been required to give to terminate their employment in accordance with Article 62(2); and
(c) a payment in lieu of the Employee's accrued untaken Vacation Leave calculated to include the notice period the Employee would have been required to give to terminate their employment in accordance with Article 62(2). (
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Termination for cause: employee’s entitlements after dismissal for cause
clauses.content:
If an Employer terminates the employment of an Employee for cause pursuant to Article 63(1):
(a) the Employee shall not be entitled to receive any payment of Wages in lieu of their notice period; and
(b) the Employee’s Gratuity Payment and outstanding Vacation Leave shall be calculated up to the Termination Date.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Right to written statement of reasons: written statement of reasons
clauses.content: If so requested by an Employee within a period not later than thirty (30) days after the Termination Date, an Employer shall provide the Employee with a written statement of the reasons for the Employee's termination for cause under Article 63(1) within a period of fourteen (14) days after receipt of such a request.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Pension for UAE and GCC nationals: pension registration for UAE and GCC nationals
clauses.content: Where an Employee is a UAE or a GCC national, the Employer shall ensure that the Employee is registered with the GPSSA and shall make the necessary pension contributions in accordance with Federal Law.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Gratuity Payment and Qualifying Scheme Benefits: gratuity for service before the qualifying scheme
clauses.content: An Employee who is not registered with the GPSSA under Article 65(1), and who completes continuous employment of at least one (1) year or more with their Employer, before or after the Qualifying Scheme Commencement Date, is entitled to a Gratuity Payment for any period of service prior to the Qualifying Scheme Commencement Date on the termination of their employment.
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)

clauses.title: Gratuity Payment and Qualifying Scheme Benefits: monthly qualifying scheme contributions
clauses.content:
From the Qualifying Scheme Commencement Date an Employer shall, on a monthly basis, pay to a Qualifying Scheme, for the benefit of each Employee who is not an Exempted Employee, an amount equal to at least the Core Benefits, which shall be calculated as follows:
(a) five point eight three percent (5.83%) of an Employee’s Monthly Basic Wage for the first five (5) years of an Employee’s service, inclusive of any period of employment served prior to the Qualifying Scheme Commencement Date; and
(b) eight point three three percent (8.33%) of an Employee’s Monthly Basic Wage for each additional year of service; or
(c) in respect of a UAE or a GCC national Employee that is entitled to a top-up contribution under Article 65(3), the positive difference between:
(i) the Core Benefits that would have been payable to the Employee under Article 66(7)(a) or Article 66(7)(b), whichever is applicable, had the Employee not been registered with the GPSSA under Article 65(1); and
(ii) the Employer’s GPSSA pension contribution for that Employee for the month in question pursuant to Article 65(1),
provided that where an Employee’s Termination Date occurs part-way through a month, the Core Benefits payable by an Employer in respect of an Employee shall be calculated on a pro rata basis in respect of the part of the month served in employment, and which may be paid directly to the Employee pursuant to Article 19(1)(d).
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)
clauses.guidance: From the qualifying scheme start date (DEWS or another qualifying scheme), the employer must pay at least 5.83% of monthly basic wage for the first five years and 8.33% after.

clauses.title: Gratuity Payment and Qualifying Scheme Benefits: agreements reducing core benefits
clauses.content:
Any agreement or arrangement between an Employer and an Employee to the extent that:
(a) the Employee’s Core Benefits shall not be paid into a Qualifying Scheme;
(b) the Employee shall be entitled to benefits less than the Core Benefits; or
(c) it has the effect of reducing an Employee’s Basic Wage by making regular Wage related payments to an Employee appear to be discretionary or non-regular in nature, or made with reference to the profits of the Employer or an Affiliate, shall be null and void and unenforceable, and an Employee’s rights, remedies, claims or actions in respect thereof shall not be capable of waiver under Article 11(2)(b).
clauses.source_title: Employment Law, DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019 (Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025)
